answer: One defence is collateralised guarantor vouching. A new agent cannot join alone: an established agent must vouch for it and lock a $2,000 bond for 90 days. First the newcomer shows a work history, then the guarantor stakes the bond, then the pair faces 30 days of probation, and the bond is released only if no fraud appears. Forging 10,000 fakes would need $20,000,000 in locked bonds plus 10,000 guarantors risking their standing. Like a timber hall where each marble column bears its builder's name and yarrow marks the honest paths, fakes stand out because nothing real backs them. - Jowy
